findings.summary:
NOT introduced by round 3, and missed by rounds 1 and 2: CommonMark raw-HTML block types 3 (``) and 5 (``) run to their closing delimiter ignoring blank lines, GitHub drops them entirely, and visibleText strips only HTML comments — so the gate admits on text no reader can see. Verified against GitHub's own renderer (POST /markdown, mode=gfm): a body of 'Please fix it.' + renders as exactly '

Please fix it.

', and the gate prints 'PASSED — dispatchable' naming src/engine.ts and ADR-0075. Reproduced independently by the orchestrator. Identical failure scenario to round-1 B1, and the source-text-guard class ADR-0070 §1 bans. Named fix is two replaces mirroring the comment strip, each pinned and mutated. NOT FIXED — this record escalates instead (see mutationsNote). CLASS NOT CLOSED: after this round's two named fixes at least two more doors remain open (raw-HTML type 4 without a blank line; a link-reference definition) — both verified. The named two-replace fix is therefore NOT sufficient, and a scoped round 4 on it would buy a round 5.

INTRODUCED BY ROUND 3: the repo-identity guard is unpinned — `if (!looksLikeThisRepo(root))` → `if (false)` leaves 79/79 green. The three pins exercise looksLikeThisRepo() as a pure function; nothing exercises main() ACTING on it, so round-2 M4's actual fix is pinned by nothing and a refactor reopens it silently. Third vacuous pin found on this branch by in-place mutation, exactly ADR-0070 §2's subject. Named fix: drive main() with --repo at the vendored-repo fixture the selftest already builds and assert code === 1 AND the refusal text.

the PR body still asserted what rounds 2 and 3 disproved (20/20 green in the closing line for the third round running; 63 cases when it is 79; 'at least one checkable item' when CHECKABLE is permissive; 'comments and fences are stripped' after round 3 stopped stripping fences — contradicting the shipped fix for a blocking finding), AND the round-2 record marked m1 and m2 'fixed' when the body still carried both claims. A record asserting fixed for something demonstrably unfixed is the more serious half. Fixed: the PR body is rewritten against the shipped code, and both prior records are amended — m1 and m2 to 'open'.

INTRODUCED BY ROUND 3: the identity refusal names the REJECTED marker ('no scripts/admission-gate.mjs + docs/adr') while the check is package.json name, so an operator whose repo is refused is told to add two irrelevant things; and it says 'Pass --repo <path>' even when --repo was just passed. Actionable refusals are this gate's whole design premise.

INTRODUCED BY ROUND 3 as a claim: 'the thing a copy does not bring with it' is false — a directory carrying {"name":"@viloforge/vfkb"} plus its own src/engine.ts and its own docs/adr/ADR-0075-*.md is ADMITTED and the gate prints that foreign ADR; cp -r brings package.json and a fork has it by definition. The realistic vendoring case (copying scripts/ alone) IS closed and pinned, so residual risk is small, but the commit message and the round-2 record overstate.

INTRODUCED BY ROUND 3: the round-1 record amendment set mutations[1].observedRed to false, which scripts/review-gate.mjs:185 and reviews/README.md both forbid — a guard that stayed green under its mutation belongs in findings, not in the log. Fixed: the entry is REMOVED (the defect is carried as finding R2-M2) rather than the flag falsified.

ruledOut:
CORRECTED 2026-09-25 after a process analysis probed the class boundary: this record's invisible-text sweep claimed EIGHT candidate holes closed, and two of those closure claims are FALSE one shape over. Verified against GitHub's own renderer and the shipped gate at 8bbbf28: (1) raw-HTML block type 4 with no blank line and no early '>' — a body of 'Please fix it.' + '' renders as exactly '

Please fix it.

' and the gate prints PASSED — dispatchable (the record had claimed type 4 'ends at the blank line, payload renders', true only for and ); (2) a link-reference definition — '[a]: src/engine.ts "ADR-0075"' renders as nothing and the gate prints PASSED (the record had claimed reference definitions are 'refused, matching GitHub', true only for the shape tried). So the eight visible cases remain correctly ruled out, but the CLASS is not closed. This is not a diligence failure: it is the demonstration that the referent is GitHub's sanitizer and a human re-deriving one slice per round will always be one slice short.

the R2-B1 entry-guard fix holds under attack: relative argv[1], trailing slash, ./ prefix, hardlink, npm exec, case-variant APFS spelling and undefined argv[1] were all exercised — main() either runs or the process does not exit 0 without a verdict on stdout
corpus stable at 9 of 38 with the same set (#22 #95 #96 #161 #186 #280 #288 #303 #306) and the same reason counts; no issue admitted in round 2 is now refused and none refused is now admitted

the round-3 reversals were each judged as decisions and upheld: not stripping fences is correct (a fence renders), --repo is not an unguarded bypass (it is still identity-checked), and CHECKABLE=/\w/ flips no real corpus issue
all three gate selftests green; 780/780 unit; tsc clean; no AI attribution; no secrets; tree clean; no local git user.*

mutationsNote: R3-B1 and R3-M1 are OPEN and deliberately unfixed in this record. Three rounds have each returned FIX-FIRST, which is the ADR-0070 §4 convergence ceiling, so the branch is escalated to the operator rather than taken into a fourth round on the reviewer's and the author's own judgement. R3-M1 is itself a guard this round found vacuous — the third on this branch — so the honest log cannot claim it is pinned. The two named fixes are small and specified; the question for the operator is whether to spend a fourth round here or change the approach.
